_what: What the reader on this computer offers to put in the person's browsers, and where each browser takes an offer (offer-in-browsers.mjs). `offers`: each browser extension Trillion makes, by its store id and the address the browser fetches it from. `browsers`: each browser by the app that shows it is installed (`app`), the folder its profiles live in (`profiles`, under which `<profile>/Extensions/<id>` means it is already there) and the folder it reads offers from (`offers_from`, under `profiles`), where one small file per extension makes the browser ask the person whether to add it the next time it opens. A browser the person never installed is passed over; a browser already holding the extension is left alone; each offer is made once per browser (kept in the reader's state folder), so an extension the person turned down is never offered again. A new extension or browser is one row. The Mac app runs `offer-in-browsers.mjs offer` (macos/computer-reader.json `children` row `browser-offers`), the same pass the reader made, which keeps a removal of the native hosts. `native_hosts`: each program this computer carries that Trillion's extensions may call directly (chrome.runtime.sendNativeMessage), by its host `name`, the carried `entry` (beside this file) the browser starts through a launcher kept in `native_host_launchers`, the `offers` whose extension ids are the only `allowed_origins` (pinned exactly), and the `actions` it answers (browser-native-host.mjs); an action that needs the person's Trillion is also a `door_actions` row { address, method }, answered by the engine's door (`engine_door`), the browser's message giving only its `input` and `request_key`. Each installed browser with `native_hosts_from` gets one manifest there; `most_message_bytes` bounds a message from the browser. `state_file` (under the home folder) is where offers made and a removal of the native hosts are kept.

engine_door._what: Where a native host's `door_actions` ask the person's own engine (engine-door.mjs): MCP `tools/call` of `do_one_thing_in_my_account` at http://127.0.0.1:<port>`path`, the port read from the private descriptor the Mac app adopts its engine with (`adoption_file`, under the home folder; macos/computer-reader.json `local_runtime.adoption_file` under Application Support), signed with the account key the Mac app's key store keeps in this Mac's Keychain item `keychain_item` (macos/App/ComputerReader.swift reads the same item, named by computer-sources.json `keychain_item`). The key is read at the call and held only in memory. The relay door's port is the one this computer's own report names (`computer_report`, the file the Mac app renders from its row, macos/computer-reader.json; `report.local_ports`), and the relay's key's public half is asked of the vault through this same door (`secrets:public`). A request is bounded by `most_request_bytes`, an answer by `most_answer_bytes` (the browser's 1 MB), the wait by `timeout_seconds`.

native_hosts.name: ai.gettrillion.computer
native_hosts.description: Lets Trillion's Send to Trillion extension ask this computer which computer it is, and read the person's lists from their Trillion on this computer.
